decision.title: Running compiled Schematron: the pattern walk visits only what a rule may match (packet )
decision.summary: A compiled Schematron pattern's visits element children always and other node kinds only when a rule context of the pattern may match them.

body.p: , after , and ("Left": validating the compiled schema costs twice what the pre-compiled XSLT's transform does on the same invoice). No public header changed; no shared file changed (only src/schematron_build.c and tests/schematron_test.c). Glossary: .

item.p: Whom it serves: every Schematron validation, first EN 16931's (sxml validate --schematron, the host's Schematron.validate). Pays: one loop over each rule context's pattern AST at compile time; no new mechanism (the walk is still xsl:apply-templates in the current mode).

Profile (callgrind, release, at a7a8d50ee; the invoice ubl-tc434-example1.xml): sxml_schematron_validate_node 1.208 x 10^9 instructions, the official stylesheet's sxml_xslt_stylesheet_transform 0.548. The C profiles have the same shape (sxml_machine_step_expression 16 % of each, the rest the machine's tasks and values), so the difference is in how much IR runs. Counted by a scratch-only hook in the evaluator (not committed), by function: steps in match functions 2,503,052 against 928,554, in template functions 73,075 against 71,402 (the rule templates, with their finding items and fired-rule checks, cost the same); calls of match functions 123,282 against 44,422, of template functions 3,541 against 1,321. By IR kind the steps scale alike (LET 1.49 M against 0.59 M, ATOM 0.35 M against 0.13 M, CONDITIONAL 0.58 M against 0.21 M, STATIC_CALL 0.13 M against 0.05 M). The match functions themselves are the same IR in both (the same patterns lowered alike).

Explanation: the evaluator chooses a template rule by calling the mode's match functions in rule order until one is true (6.8), so a visit costs about one call per rule of the mode for a node no rule matches. 's walk applied templates to @* | node(), so each of the three modes visited 1,177 nodes of the invoice (369 elements, 70 attributes, 738 text nodes, 516 of them whitespace only) and every text node tried every rule in vain; the ISO skeleton walks @* | *, 439 nodes per mode. 2.7 times the visits gave 2.8 times the match calls and the factor 2.2.

Mechanism (src/schematron_build.c): the pattern walk selects the element children always, and attributes, text, comment and processing-instruction children only when a rule context of the pattern may match that node kind; other nodes are unobservable, as no rule of the pattern can match them. The kinds come from the context's pattern AST, read as XSLT 4.0, 6.3 matches: the last step of a path (after "/", "//", a rooted variable), both sides of a union, the left of intersect and except, the value of a filter, the inside of parentheses; an axis step's node test gives its kind, a name test or wildcard the principal node kind of its axis (XPath 4.0, 4.6.4.1); "/" a document node; every other pattern (node(), $v, id(), key(), ., simple patterns, an expression rule context wrapped as .[...]) may match any kind. A loop over the nodes and their ancestors (). The walks are added after the pattern's rules, once every context is known: the traversal templates are now declared after the rules (priority -1 orders them last, as before), and each rule template's walk is appended as its last instruction. 's semantics are unchanged: a rule that can match a node still sees it, the first matching rule wins in a pattern, every rule of a group fires, phases, from and documents choose the start as before, let once per context node, both locations, value-of as fn:string. EN 16931's contexts are all elements: its walk is *.

Measured (callgrind, release; base a7a8d50ee and the change built alike from snapshots). Invoice: validation 1.208 to 0.479 x 10^9 (the official stylesheet's transform 0.548), the whole validate --schematron 2.633 to 1.903, the compile unchanged (1.405 to 1.404); template calls 3,541 to 1,111, match calls 123,282 to 36,612. The 1,131 VEFA instances (sxml-schematron-test vefa, compile and all validations): 49.90 to 29.03 x 10^9, validation 47.14 to 26.27. Seconds (processor, a shared 4-CPU machine): invoice fastest of 15, interleaved, 0.362 to 0.296 (the official stylesheet's transform 0.258, its compile included); VEFA validation 7.51 to 4.65 s; the 1,150 files of 's comparison in one sxml validate run 9.8 to 5.3 s.

Same result: sxml validate --format=json over EN 16931's 1,131 UBL unit test instances (each <test>'s document, extracted as the VEFA harness does) and the 19 UBL examples, all in one run: 14.8 MB, byte-identical. 7.30's suite through sxml-schematron-test: 463 of 463 applicable, 3 deviations, 43 implementation-defined, 5 not applicable, as before; EN 16931 UBL 1,133 of 1,133 checks. A new unit test, pattern_walk_reaches_every_kind_a_rule_matches, has a pattern per kind (elements, @n, text(), a comment step after a parenthesized step, a processing instruction, node() except *, an expression rule context) and checks every report in order. debug-gcc: the whole suite passes (459 tests; kotlin/jvm and swift/linux skipped); clang-tidy clean on both files; tools/check-call-cycles.py finds no cycle. QT4 and XT40 were not run: no shared file changed.

Left (see "## Proposed"): a rule search that skips rules whose pattern cannot match the item's node kind or name would help every stylesheet with many rules, the official EN 16931 one as much as this.
